- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early after sharp spikes in history, then drop too quickly — underestimating subsequent volatility.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model holds prices near forecasted mean too long, ignoring true price swings.
- Overshoots after spikes are common — model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, then fails to adjust downward.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–10 days) are often too low, suggesting model underweights tail risks or ignores recent downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to true price drops — often misses sudden corrections by 1–3 days.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in mid-to-late period, especially when true prices show downward trend or consolidation.
- Model underestimates volatility in late cycles — fails to account for sudden spikes or sharp reversals near end of forecast horizon.
